name: PM-KISAN Samman Nidhi (Demo)
shortDescription: Direct income support of ₹6,000 per year transferred in three equal installments to eligible landholding farmer families.
overview: A central sector demonstration summary illustrating direct income supplementation to small and marginal agricultural households to support input procurement and seasonal crop expenses.
benefits: ₹6,000 per year disbursed in three equal installments of ₹2,000 every four months.
Direct bank transfer via Aadhaar-linked Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT).
Helps cover seasonal seed, fertilizer, and domestic agricultural expenses.
eligibilityConditions: Cultivable landholding farmer families as recorded in state/UT land registries.
Applicant must be an Indian citizen aged 18 years or above.
Mandatory Aadhaar e-KYC and Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
applicationProcedure: Verify land record entry and complete Aadhaar e-KYC.
Submit farmer registration details through pmkisan.gov.in or nearest Common Service Centre (CSC).
Track state-level verification and installment release status using registration ID.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Institutional landholders are excluded.
Former and present holders of constitutional posts, serving/retired government officers, and income tax payers in the last assessment year are excluded.
Professionals such as doctors, engineers, lawyers, and chartered accountants registered with professional bodies are excluded.

sourceDocument.sourceLabel: Demonstration record from official pmkisan.gov.in summary

versionHistory.changeSummary: Initial demonstration record seeded from official portal overview.

criteria.note: Requires cultivable agricultural landholding status in official records.

name: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY (Demo)
shortDescription: Cashless secondary and tertiary hospitalization coverage up to ₹5 lakh per family per year across empanelled hospitals.
overview: Demonstration summary of India’s flagship public health assurance program providing cashless treatment coverage for eligible economically vulnerable households.
benefits: Health cover up to ₹5,00,000 per family per year for secondary and tertiary care hospitalization.
Covers pre-hospitalization diagnostics (3 days) and post-hospitalization follow-up (15 days).
Paperless and cashless access at empanelled public and private hospitals nationwide.
eligibilityConditions: Households listed under SECC deprivation categories or holding eligible state-linked ration/BPL cards.
No cap on family size or member age under scheme rules.
Senior citizens aged 70+ qualify under expanded senior citizen coverage.
applicationProcedure: Check family inclusion status via beneficiary.nha.gov.in.
Visit nearest empanelled hospital Ayushman Mitra desk or CSC for Aadhaar e-KYC.
Download Ayushman card upon verification for cashless admission.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Covers inpatient hospitalization packages; routine OPD consultations without admission are generally excluded.
Cosmetic procedures and non-listed experimental treatments are excluded.

versionHistory.changeSummary: Initial demonstration record seeded from official portal overview.

criteria.note: Primarily targeted at socio-economically eligible households or senior citizens.

name: National Post-Matric Scholarship (Demo)
shortDescription: Tuition fee reimbursement and monthly academic maintenance allowance for students enrolled in post-matriculation studies.
overview: Demonstration entry representing central scholarship assistance designed to reduce financial drop-out barriers for students pursuing Class 11, diploma, undergraduate, and postgraduate programs.
benefits: Reimbursement of compulsory non-refundable institutional tuition fees.
Annual maintenance allowance for hostellers and day scholars.
Direct disbursement into the student’s Aadhaar-seeded bank account.
eligibilityConditions: Student enrolled in a recognized post-matriculation or post-secondary institution.
Annual household income below ₹2,50,000 across all sources (varies by specific scholarship sub-scheme).
Minimum qualifying academic percentage and attendance compliance.
applicationProcedure: Register on the National Scholarship Portal (scholarships.gov.in) and generate an OTR ID.
Complete academic profile and upload scanned supporting certificates.
Submit form for institute nodal verification and state/central sanction.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Students cannot simultaneously avail two central post-matric scholarships for the same academic year.
Failure to maintain minimum attendance or passing promotion may halt renewal.

targetBeneficiaries: EWS / SC / ST / OBC / Minority Students
criteria.note: Requires active enrollment in a recognized post-matric course.

name: Pradhan Mantri Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0 (Demo)
shortDescription: Interest subsidy and direct financial assistance for EWS and LIG urban families building or purchasing their first pucca home.
overview: Demonstration summary illustrating urban affordable housing support through Beneficiary-Led Construction and Interest Subsidy components.
benefits: Interest subsidy or central construction grant up to ₹2.50 lakh for eligible urban households.
Promotes female co-ownership or sole ownership of assisted housing units.
Supports both new house construction and eligible home purchase.
eligibilityConditions: Beneficiary family must not own a pucca house anywhere in India.
Annual household income up to ₹3,00,000 (EWS) or ₹6,00,000 (LIG).
Applicant must reside in a notified statutory town or urban local body area.
applicationProcedure: Review income bracket and check municipal urban local body eligibility.
Submit online assessment via pmaymis.gov.in or municipal facilitation desk.
Complete geo-tagged site or loan verification with participating bank/ULB.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Families who have already availed central/state housing assistance under prior housing missions are ineligible.
Property must be located within notified urban planning boundaries.

criteria.note: Applicant household must not already own a permanent (pucca) residence.

name: Pradhan Mantri MUDRA Yojana (Demo)
shortDescription: Collateral-free micro-enterprise loans across Shishu, Kishore, and Tarun tiers up to ₹20 lakh for non-farm small businesses.
overview: Demonstration record outlining institutional credit access for micro-enterprises, artisans, shopkeepers, and small service providers through commercial banks and MFIs.
benefits: Collateral-free term loans and working capital from ₹50,000 (Shishu) up to ₹20,00,000 (Tarun Plus).
No third-party collateral security required under Credit Guarantee framework.
Supports machinery purchase, inventory expansion, and small commercial operations.
eligibilityConditions: Indian citizen aged 18+ with a viable non-farm income-generating business plan.
Clean credit history with no prior willful loan default.
Available to sole proprietors, partnership firms, and small service enterprises.
applicationProcedure: Prepare a concise business profile and projected cash flow summary.
Apply via JanSamarth portal or approach nearest scheduled commercial bank / RRB.
Complete KYC and credit appraisal for loan sanction.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Strictly intended for non-farm manufacturing, trading, and service micro-enterprises (direct crop farming loans are outside MUDRA).
Tarun Plus tier (₹10–20 lakh) applies to entrepreneurs who successfully repaid earlier Tarun loans.

criteria.note: Requires a non-farm micro or small business activity.

name: DAY-NRLM Lakhpati Didi Initiative (Demo)
shortDescription: Livelihood training, revolving credit, and market linkage support for rural women Self-Help Group (SHG) members.
overview: Demonstration entry showcasing rural women enterprise enablement aimed at helping SHG households reach sustainable annual incomes above ₹1 lakh.
benefits: Interest-subvented SHG working capital and enterprise startup support.
Hands-on vocational, financial literacy, and digital bookkeeping training.
Market access support for rural crafts, dairy, poultry, and agro-processing.
eligibilityConditions: Women residing in rural areas who are active members of a recognized Self-Help Group.
Age generally between 18 and 55 years.
Household annual income below ₹3,00,000 in sample guidelines.
applicationProcedure: Join or verify membership in a village-level Self-Help Group under SRLM.
Submit a household livelihood plan through the Block Mission Management Unit.
Access training and SHG credit disbursement upon cluster approval.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Restricted to rural households organized within registered DAY-NRLM Self-Help Groups.

criteria.note: Designed for rural women participating in Self-Help Groups.

name: Atal Pension Yojana (Demo)
shortDescription: Guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 after age 60 based on regular subscriber contributions.
overview: Demonstration overview of a voluntary contributory pension scheme focused on workers in the unorganized sector to secure predictable post-retirement income.
benefits: Guaranteed minimum monthly pension between ₹1,000 and ₹5,000 upon turning 60.
Spouse continues to receive the same pension after the subscriber’s lifetime.
Nominee receives accumulated corpus after both subscriber and spouse.
eligibilityConditions: Indian citizen aged between 18 and 40 years.
Active savings bank account or post office savings account.
Subscriber must not be an income tax payer at enrollment.
requiredDocuments: Mobile Number linked with Bank Account
applicationProcedure: Visit your bank branch or enable enrollment through net-banking APY portal.
Select desired pension slab (₹1,000 to ₹5,000) and auto-debit frequency.
Receive Permanent Retirement Account Number (PRAN) confirmation.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Income tax payers are ineligible to join APY.
Premature exit before age 60 is permitted only under exceptional circumstances.

criteria.note: Entry age window is strictly 18–40 years; excludes income tax payers.

name: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension (Demo)
shortDescription: Monthly non-contributory pension support for senior citizens aged 60 and above from BPL households.
overview: Demonstration summary of social assistance under NSAP providing basic monthly financial security to elderly citizens in economically vulnerable households.
benefits: Central monthly pension component enhanced with state top-up grants (varies by state).
Higher pension slab automatically applicable for citizens aged 80 years and above.
Direct credit into senior citizen bank or post office account.
eligibilityConditions: Citizen aged 60 years or older.
Household listed under Below Poverty Line (BPL) criteria prescribed by the state.
Not receiving overlapping statutory old-age pension benefits.
applicationProcedure: Obtain age verification and BPL status verification from local Gram Panchayat or Urban Local Body.
Submit NSAP application through state social welfare office or UMANG portal.
Receive monthly DBT credit upon district sanction.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Restricted strictly to BPL households as defined by state/central criteria.

criteria.note: Requires age 60+ and BPL eligibility verification.

name: PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana 4.0 (Demo)
shortDescription: Free industry-aligned vocational training, certification, and placement assistance for youth across technical and service trades.
overview: Demonstration record describing short-term skill certification and Recognition of Prior Learning (RPL) programs aimed at improving youth employability.
benefits: 100% tuition-free short-term skill training at accredited Skill India centers.
Nationally recognized NSQF certification upon assessment.
Placement support, apprenticeship linkage, and career counseling.
eligibilityConditions: Indian youth generally aged 15 to 45 years.
School/college dropouts or unemployed youth seeking industry-ready certification.
Valid Aadhaar and bank account for tracking assessment support.
applicationProcedure: Browse accredited Skill India Digital Hub courses and select a trade.
Enroll at a nearby Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Kendra (PMKK) with Aadhaar verification.
Complete training hours and pass practical assessment for certification.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Candidates must fulfill minimum attendance requirements to qualify for final assessment certification.

criteria.note: Open to youth and workers seeking NSQF-aligned vocational skills.

name: MGNREGA Rural Wage Guarantee (Demo)
shortDescription: Guarantees up to 100 days of unskilled manual wage employment per financial year to rural households.
overview: Demonstration summary of statutory rural livelihood security focusing on durable community assets, water conservation, and rural connectivity.
benefits: Up to 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per rural household annually.
Wages transferred directly to worker bank accounts within 15 days of muster roll closure.
Unemployment allowance provisions if work is not allotted within statutory window.
eligibilityConditions: Adult members of any rural household willing to undertake unskilled manual work.
Applicant must be 18 years or older and reside in the respective Gram Panchayat.
applicationProcedure: Apply for a Job Card at the local Gram Panchayat office.
Submit written or digital demand for work once Job Card is issued.
Report to allotted worksite and receive direct wage credit.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Applicable strictly to rural Gram Panchayat jurisdictions; urban municipal areas are excluded.

criteria.note: Exclusively applicable to rural Gram Panchayat residents.

name: PM SVANidhi Street Vendor Credit (Demo)
shortDescription: Affordable working capital micro-loans starting at ₹10,000 with interest subsidy and digital cashback incentives for urban street vendors.
overview: Demonstration summary of micro-credit restoration and digital payment onboarding for urban street vendors, hawkers, and small stall operators.
benefits: Progressive collateral-free working capital loans of ₹10,000, ₹20,000, and ₹50,000.
7% annual interest subsidy on timely repayment.
Monthly digital transaction cashback incentives.
eligibilityConditions: Urban street vendors holding Certificate of Vending or Letter of Recommendation from Urban Local Body.
Age 18 years or older engaged in urban vending activities.
applicationProcedure: Verify vendor survey listing or request Letter of Recommendation from Urban Local Body.
Submit loan application via pmsvanidhi.mohua.gov.in or nearest Common Service Centre.
Complete lender KYC to receive working capital disbursement.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Second and third loan tranches require timely full repayment of the previous tranche.

name: ADIP & Divyangjan Assistance Scheme (Demo)
department: Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
shortDescription: Financial assistance for modern assistive devices, mobility aids, and rehabilitation support for persons with benchmark disabilities.
overview: Demonstration record outlining targeted social welfare assistance to improve independent living and educational/vocational access for citizens with disabilities.
benefits: Subsidized or free modern assistive aids and prosthetic devices.
Supports motorized tricycles, hearing aids, and smart educational tools based on income slab.
Linked with Unique Disability ID (UDID) for streamlined state and central benefits.
eligibilityConditions: Indian citizen with 40% or more certified benchmark disability.
Monthly household income generally up to ₹22,500 for 100% grant (50% grant up to ₹30,000/month).
applicationProcedure: Apply for a Unique Disability ID (UDID) on the Swavlamban portal.
Attend district medical assessment camp or ALIMCO distribution center.
Receive approved assistive equipment upon verification.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Repeat issuance of identical assistive devices is subject to standard replacement period rules (typically 3 years).

criteria.note: Requires certified benchmark disability (40% or above).

name: Mukhyamantri Majhi Ladki Bahin Yojana (Demo)
shortDescription: Monthly direct financial support of ₹1,500 to eligible women aged 21–65 in Maharashtra for household economic independence.
overview: State-level demonstration example showing direct financial assistance aimed at nutrition, health, and financial autonomy of women from low- and middle-income households in Maharashtra.
benefits: ₹1,500 per month transferred directly via Aadhaar-linked DBT.
Priority coverage for married, widowed, divorced, and destitute women in eligible families.
eligibilityConditions: Female permanent resident of Maharashtra aged 21 to 65 years.
Annual family income should not exceed ₹2,50,000.
No family member should be an income tax payer or regular government employee.
applicationProcedure: Verify Aadhaar-bank seeding and collect Maharashtra domicile or 15-year residence proof.
Submit application via state portal or Anganwadi Sevika desk.
Track district approval and monthly DBT status online.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Families owning a four-wheeler (excluding tractors) or paying income tax are excluded.
Beneficiaries already receiving ₹1,500+ under other state financial schemes are excluded.

criteria.note: Applicable to eligible women domiciled in Maharashtra.

name: Pudhumai Penn Higher Education Grant (Demo)
department: Dept. of Social Welfare, Tamil Nadu
shortDescription: Monthly ₹1,000 educational assistance for girl students from government schools pursuing undergraduate, diploma, or ITI courses.
overview: State-level demonstration entry illustrating targeted higher-education retention incentives for young women in Tamil Nadu.
benefits: ₹1,000 monthly scholarship directly to the student’s bank account until course completion.
Can be combined with standard merit scholarships in sample state policy.
eligibilityConditions: Girl students who studied Classes 6 to 12 in Tamil Nadu government schools.
Currently enrolled in an accredited diploma, ITI, or undergraduate degree program.
applicationProcedure: Verify Class 6–12 government school EMIS records through current college nodal officer.
Submit student bank details on the Tamil Nadu higher education portal.
Receive monthly allowance upon institutional verification.
restrictionsAndExceptions: Applies exclusively to female students who completed Classes 6–12 in Tamil Nadu government schools.

sourceDocument.sourceLabel: Demonstration record from Tamil Nadu Social Welfare Dept.

criteria.note: Applies to female students in Tamil Nadu who attended Classes 6–12 in government schools.
